draft.title: Programs for youth health
card: A health program is a planned set of actions that aims to improve the health of a group. Youth health programs aim at young people, for example by cutting road injuries or supporting mental health.
run or funded by a government, such as a state road safety campaign. Governments can reach large numbers of people, and they draw on public money.
run by a group outside government, such as a charity or community organisation. It may be funded by donations, or by grants from government.
Programs often target an area where health data shows young people need help. A program can be judged by asking who it aims to reach and whether it improves health for them.
draft.remember: A youth health program is a planned effort to improve young people's health, run by government or by other groups.

a.q: Which of these is a non-government youth health program?
opts: A charity runs free mental health talks at local schools
A state agency airs a TV ad about drink driving
A state education department adds health to school classes
A council uses its own funds to build a youth clinic
a.why: A charity is outside government, so its program is non-government. The other three are run by a government body, so they are government programs. Funding does not decide it: a charity may even receive a government grant.
a.clue: Look for who runs the program, not who it helps.

b.q: A state government pays a youth charity to run a peer-led mental health program in country towns. What is the best description of this program?
opts: A non-government program, as the charity runs it
A government program, as the government pays for it
A government program, as it is aimed at young people
A non-government program, as it is aimed at country towns
b.why: The charity runs the program, so it is a non-government program, even though a government grant pays for it. Government funding alone does not make a program a government one. Who the program is aimed at does not decide the type either.
b.clue: Ask who runs the program, not who pays for it.

a.best: A charity runs free mental health talks at local schools

b.best: A non-government program, as the charity runs it
also_right: A government program, as the government pays for it
